person.name: Priyanka Nitin Bhorkar
person.title: SAP HANA & BI/BW Developer, M.Sc. Web Engineering student
person.headline: SAP HANA and BI/BW developer, now studying Web Engineering
person.intro: Over four years of building finance data models and BI reporting at Deloitte and Accenture. Now an M.Sc. Web Engineering student at TU Chemnitz, bringing that enterprise data background to web and cloud applications.
person.summary: M.Sc. Web Engineering student at Chemnitz University of Technology with over 4 years of experience as an SAP HANA Developer and SAP BI/BW Consultant. Experienced in implementation, migration, and support projects, with a strong focus on data modelling, BI reporting, and system optimization.
person.seeking: A Werkstudent role where she can apply her enterprise data expertise and her current studies in web engineering to modern web and cloud solutions.

about: From SAP BW process chains to SAP HANA Calculation Views, I spent over four years as an SAP BI/BW Consultant at Accenture and an SAP HANA Developer at Deloitte. I designed the finance reporting layer and cut report load time (by approx. 50%), and automated 26 month-end activities with Blue Prism RPA (approx. 50 hours saved per month).

Now pursuing my M.Sc. in Web Engineering at TU Chemnitz, I build with Python, FastAPI and PostgreSQL. I am seeking a Werkstudent role where my background in enterprise data and my studies in web engineering come together in modern web and cloud solutions.

experience.title: Analyst, SAP HANA Developer
experience.summary: Designed the SAP HANA data models and Calculation Views behind finance reporting, from data loading to the report itself.

projects.name: German Road Accident Data Platform
projects.tagline: Open government accident data integrated into one PostgreSQL database, served through a documented API and a dashboard.
projects.description: Built a full-stack platform that integrates open government data (Unfallatlas, regional indicators, AGS/GV-ISys keys) into a single PostgreSQL database through an ETL pipeline. A documented FastAPI service (Swagger/OpenAPI) offers filtering and cross-source statistics, such as fatal-accident and bicycle-risk rankings by district, and returns data-licence metadata (DL-DE-BY-2.0) with its responses. A Streamlit dashboard with 5 views, including regional accident rates and an accident explorer, makes the data easy to explore.

detail.context: A full-stack platform built on open government data about road accidents in Germany.
detail.challenge: The data comes from separate sources (Unfallatlas, regional indicators, AGS/GV-ISys keys) that have to be brought together before they can be compared.
detail.role: Built the platform: ETL pipeline, database, API and dashboard.
detail.approach: Integrate every source into a single PostgreSQL database through an ETL pipeline, then expose it through an API and a dashboard.
technical: ETL pipeline loading Unfallatlas data, regional indicators and AGS/GV-ISys keys into PostgreSQL
FastAPI service documented with Swagger/OpenAPI, with filtering and cross-source statistics such as fatal-accident and bicycle-risk rankings by district
Streamlit dashboard with 5 views, including regional accident rates and an accident explorer
Data-licence metadata (DL-DE-BY-2.0) returned with API responses
detail.result: A working platform with a documented API and a five-view dashboard over one integrated database.

projects.name: Attribute Naming Convention Analyzer
projects.tagline: A data quality tool that checks how consistently the columns of a dataset are named.
projects.description: Built a data quality tool that analyses column naming in CSV and JSON datasets. It detects 9 naming styles, including snake_case, camelCase and PascalCase, and flags ambiguous attributes. It calculates the dominant style and a consistency percentage, shows them on an interactive dashboard with KPI cards and charts, and exports the results as a PDF report.

detail.context: A data quality tool for CSV and JSON datasets.
detail.challenge: Datasets mix naming styles and contain ambiguous attribute names, which is hard to judge by eye.
detail.role: Built the tool: analysis logic, dashboard and report export.
detail.approach: Classify every column name by style, then measure how consistent the dataset is as a whole.
technical: Detects 9 naming styles, including snake_case, camelCase and PascalCase
Calculates the dominant style and a consistency percentage
Interactive Streamlit dashboard with KPI cards and charts
detail.result: A working tool that reports a dataset's dominant naming style and consistency percentage, with a PDF report to share.
